nodes.label: PTZ Camera Autotracking
nodes.rationale: Requires ONVIF RelativePanTiltTranslationSpace with a TranslationSpaceFov entry; cameras that only claim support (or never update MoveStatus, as with many Hikvision firmwares) cannot be worked around and autotracking is disabled.

nodes.label: PTZ Calibration and movement_weights
nodes.rationale: Calibration measures PTZ motor speed over a series of moves so Frigate can predict how far to move to recenter an object. The UI and other cameras are intentionally unresponsive during calibration to avoid excessive network and CPU load. Weights keep refining at runtime, so calibrate_on_startup must be turned off afterwards or the refined values are overwritten.

nodes.label: Autotracking Zoom Modes
nodes.rationale: Absolute zoom is conservative and separate from pan/tilt because it works on the widest range of cameras; relative zoom moves concurrently but ONVIF makes no guarantee about how the generic zoom range maps to magnification, so behavior varies by vendor. A high zoom_factor starves the motion estimator of background detail and loses the object.

nodes.label: PTZ Motion Estimator
nodes.rationale: Tracked objects are preserved across camera moves by estimating camera motion from frame detail, which is why a motion mask over the timestamp is recommended and why scenes without hard edges, motion blur, or an over-zoomed object break tracking.
